title: Price-aware nitrogen advice for monsoon rice, delivered through existing digital advisory channels
user: Rice farmers (via advisory app/extension); advisory providers
decision: How much urea to apply, and when, given this season's urea and paddy prices, zone and establishment method
required_information: Plot yield response to N by zone and establishment method; current urea and expected paddy prices; shock risk
analysis: Yield-response functions (quadratic-plateau) estimated on MAPS panel with household fixed effects and weather/conflict controls → economic optimum N at price ratio → simple lookup table
action: Advisory recommends a rate band and split timing each season
expected_outcome: Higher profit per acre and N use efficiency; avoided losses from over/under-application

score_notes.importance: Fertilizer is the main commercial input; prices up 23-49% (S302,S304)
score_notes.data_availability: MAPS rounds 1-8 public with plot inputs and yields
score_notes.implementation_feasibility: Existing app reaches 139,000 farmers (S298); RCM prototype exists (S112)

pathway: Partner with an existing digital advisory provider and DoA; publish lookup tables each season
key_risk: Observational yield response confounded by farmer skill and soil - mitigated with panel FE, control-function, and an A/B validation

design.why_it_matters: Fertilizer is the single most important commercial input. Prices rose 23% (2023-2025) and another 28-49% in 2026, profits fell 40%, and conflict has eroded fertilizer use efficiency every year since 2021. A better rate decision touches nearly every rice farmer, every season.
design.research_question: What nitrogen rate (and split) maximizes expected profit per acre for monsoon rice by agro-ecological zone and establishment method at current urea:paddy price ratios, and does delivering this advice raise farmer profit?
design.hypothesis: H1: Yield response to N differs by zone, establishment method and conflict exposure, so a single national recommendation is mis-specified. H2: Price-aware advice raises profit per acre by reducing N where marginal returns are below cost and increasing it where they exceed cost.
design.target: Monsoon rice farmers in Delta, Dry Zone and Coastal zones (MAPS sample covers all states/regions)
required_data: Plot N, P, K quantities and timing
available_data: D04 MAPS rounds 1-8 (inputs, yields, prices, establishment, shocks)
D06 retail rice prices (no Delta coverage)
missing_data: Fertilizer timing detail may be limited in MAPS (verify questionnaire)

collection_plan.sampling: Stratified random subsample of advisory users (e.g., 3 townships x 30 farmers)
collection_plan.qc: Standard 2.5x2.5 m crop cuts, moisture meter

collection_plan.variable: N applied per split and date
collection_plan.sampling: All pilot users via app form

design.dependent: Yield (t/ha; converted from baskets/acre using the paddy basket weight documented by MAPS) and profit per acre
design.baseline: Descriptive N-yield curves by zone; pooled OLS quadratic response; economic optimum = where marginal product x paddy price = urea price
design.advanced: Panel fixed effects / correlated random effects with control function for N endogeneity (as in S269); justified because N is chosen by farmers. ML (e.g., causal forests) only if heterogeneity remains unexplained.
design.validation: Leave-one-round-out prediction of yields; comparison with agronomic benchmarks (S090, S114); then a randomized A/B test of advice variants inside the advisory app (outcome: crop-cut yield, N use, profit).
design.causal_note: Observational response curves are associations (better farmers apply more N). The A/B test provides causal evidence on the advice itself.
design.output: Seasonal lookup table (zone x establishment x price ratio → N band and timing) + open notebook + 4-page brief
design.intervention: Deliver as SMS/app advisory through an existing digital climate-advisory provider (I04) and DoA extension
design.decision: Farmer's N rate and timing each season
design.end_user: Rice farmers; advisory providers; DoA extension
design.impact_measurement: Change in profit per acre, N use efficiency (kg grain/kg N) and adoption rate among advised vs control users
limitations: MAPS yields are self-reported for the largest plot
Advice cannot fix fertilizer availability in cut-off areas (Rakhine)

title: Crop-establishment decision model: broadcast vs row-seeding vs transplanting under labour and water constraints
decision: Which establishment method maximizes expected profit given wage, seed, water and service availability
required_information: Yield and cost by method, zone and season; wage and fee levels
analysis: Endogenous-switching or matching estimates of method yield/profit gaps; break-even wage thresholds; service-demand map
action: Advise method by zone; identify where row-seeding services pay off
expected_outcome: Recover part of perceived broadcast yield penalty while saving labour

design.why_it_matters: Half of monsoon farmers and three-quarters of dry-season farmers now broadcast seed because labour and water are scarce; farmers believe this costs ~11 baskets/acre and 2025 yields fell as broadcasting rose.
design.research_question: Under which wage, water and service conditions does broadcasting, mechanized row/drum seeding or transplanting maximize profit?
design.hypothesis: Broadcast DSR is profit-maximizing only above a wage threshold; precision seeding dominates where services exist.
design.target: Monsoon and dry-season rice farmers nationally
design.baseline: Partial budgets by method and zone
design.advanced: Endogenous switching regression or matching to address self-selection
design.validation: Out-of-sample by round; field demonstration plots
design.causal_note: Method choice is self-selected; estimates are conditional associations unless trials are run.
design.output: Break-even wage maps and advisory rules
design.intervention: Promote row/drum seeding services via existing outsourcing providers (I01)
design.decision: Farmer's establishment method; provider investment in seeders
design.impact_measurement: Yield and profit vs broadcasting neighbours

title: Township flood-loss early estimate for Delta monsoon rice
decision: Which townships need replanting seed, relief or loss verification after a flood
required_information: Flood extent x rice area x crop stage; calibrated loss rates
analysis: Sentinel-1 flood mapping intersected with rice masks and crop calendars; loss model calibrated on MAPS township flood-shock yields

score_notes.validation_feasibility: MAPS flood shocks are self-reported and coarse

pathway: Share maps with clusters/agencies each monsoon
key_risk: Ground truth limited; cloud-free optical unavailable in monsoon (use SAR)

design.why_it_matters: Floods and heavy rain hit 7-15% of farmers per monsoon with 15-34% yield losses, yet no township-level loss estimate exists in season.
design.research_question: Can Sentinel-1 flood extent intersected with rice area predict township-level yield losses reported by farmers?
design.hypothesis: Flood duration over rice area explains a substantial share of township variation in reported flood losses.
design.dependent: Share of farmers reporting flood loss; yield loss
design.impact_measurement: Time to assistance; coverage of affected

title: Randomized evaluation of digital climate advisories for rice
required_information: Causal effect on yields and income
analysis: Randomized rollout or staggered DiD with provider

design.why_it_matters: Digital advisories are the only scaled channel (139,000 farmers) but evidence is non-random.
design.research_question: What is the causal effect of DCAS on rice yields, input use and income?
design.hypothesis: DCAS raises yields modestly (well below the reported 20%).
design.advanced: Staggered DiD if rollout not randomizable

title: Monthly rice profitability (cost-price squeeze) nowcast between survey rounds

required_information: Input price, wage, fee and paddy price trajectories by region
analysis: Seasonal farm budgets from MAPS rolled forward with monthly price indices; nowcast real profit per acre
action: Time support before planting in regions with negative margins

score_notes.novelty: IFPRI already publishes seasonal assessments - incremental

pathway: Monthly brief to donor coordination groups
key_risk: Price data gaps in main rice regions

design.why_it_matters: Profitability swings (+41% to -40%) drive input use; support is timed after the fact.
design.research_question: Can monthly prices nowcast seasonal real profit per acre by region?
design.hypothesis: Price indices explain most variation in survey-based margins.
